gloss: ritual clapping at a Shinto shrine

definitions.explanation: The ceremonial clapping performed when worshipping at a Shinto shrine, typically two claps with the palms slightly offset to produce a clear, resonant sound that calls the attention of the {神|かみ}.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{柏手|かしわで}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}った→打つ：01221_utsu⟧。
examples.english: I clapped my hands ritually at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {二礼|にれい}⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧⟦{拍手|はくしゅ}→拍手：03553_hakushu⟧⟦{一礼|いちれい}→一礼：15889_ichirei⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}って→言う：00515_iu⟧、{柏手|かしわで}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{二回|にかい}→二回：27625_nikai⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧。
examples.english: It's called "two bows, two claps, one bow," and you clap your hands twice.

examples.japanese: ⟦{出雲大社|いずもたいしゃ}→出雲大社：29110_izumotaisha⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{他|ほか}→他：04129_hoka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{違|ちが}って→違う：01957_chigau⟧{柏手|かしわで}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{四回|よんかい}⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{習|なら}わし→習わし：13910_narawashi⟧だ。
examples.english: At Izumo Taisha, unlike other shrines, the custom is to clap four times.

notes:
The kanji ⟦{柏|かしわ}→柏：26146_kashiwa⟧ (oak) is used here for historical phonetic reasons rather than meaning. Sometimes written in hiragana as かしわ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {柏手|かしわで}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: to clap ritually (the standard verb is ⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧, not the everyday ⟦{叩|たた}く→叩く：02072_tataku⟧)
- {柏手|かしわで}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧: the sound of ritual clapping
- ⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧⟦{拍手|はくしゅ}→拍手：03553_hakushu⟧: two claps (modern term for the same act)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The standard pattern at most Shinto shrines is {二礼|にれい}⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧⟦{拍手|はくしゅ}→拍手：03553_hakushu⟧⟦{一礼|いちれい}→一礼：15889_ichirei⟧: bow twice, clap twice, bow once. The right hand is positioned slightly lower than the left to produce a clearer sound. ⟦{出雲大社|いずもたいしゃ}→出雲大社：29110_izumotaisha⟧ and {宇佐神宮|うさじんぐう} use four claps instead of two.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{拍手|はくしゅ}→拍手：03553_hakushu⟧: applause; also used in the formal expression {二拍手|にはくしゅ} for ritual clapping
- ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{合|あ}わせる→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧: to put one's hands together — the gesture used at Buddhist temples instead of clapping
